# Synthetic Office fixtures

These one-page documents were generated for integration tests, using
`python-docx`, `openpyxl`, and `python-pptx`. They contain no user documents.

- `sample.docx`: heading `WORD MARKER` and one explanatory paragraph.
- `sample.xlsx`: `SHEET MARKER` in A1, with print area A1:B4.
- `sample.pptx`: one slide with a textbox containing `SLIDE MARKER`.
- `multiple-sheets.xlsx`: two visible sheets containing `FIRST SHEET` and
  `SECOND SHEET`, plus a hidden sheet containing `HIDDEN SHEET`.
- `excel-pagination.xlsx`: a wide portrait sheet with an oversized print area,
  formatting at Z100 and a manual row break; a landscape sheet using paper code
  14 with incomplete fit settings; a formatting-only sheet; and a hidden sheet.
  By default, both nonempty visible sheets export on one page each, with markers at
  their left, right and bottom edges. This reproduces blank pages, split columns
  and missing landscape content without including any user data.
- `excel-print-preview.xlsx`: a portrait sheet with four markers separated by
  manual row and column breaks, scale 100%, print area A1:D30 and down-then-over
  page order; a landscape sheet at 80% scale; and a hidden sheet. With
  `--excel-preserve-layout`, export must preserve five pages in order, omit content outside the print area, and
  leave the hidden sheet out. Automatic fitting deliberately replaces these saved print areas.
- `excel-mixed-paper.xlsx`: an A4 sheet with two printed markers, a manual row
  break and blank overflow; a sheet without an explicit paper size (Excel's
  default Letter); an image-only A4 sheet; a landscape Folio sheet; and a hidden
  sheet. `--excel-preserve-layout` keeps five nonblank pages, preserves each paper size,
  includes the last visible sheet and retains the image-only page. The Folio
  sheet has incomplete fit settings, matching the mixed-paper failure class.
- `excel-table-sections.xlsx`: two side-by-side, 90-row tables with a unique
  label/value pair in their first and last columns on every row. The test uses
  separate A1:D90 and F1:I90 print areas with width-only fitting. Each table must
  continue onto multiple pages while keeping each row's columns together.
  An outside marker is excluded and a second visible summary sheet is retained.

- `excel-auto-tables.xlsx`: automatic detection without any print-area arguments.
  Contains two 90-row tables separated by a blank gutter, two adjacent tables
  with staggered merged headings, and a single wide table with a shared heading.
  Stale saved print areas intentionally omit data. The default must retain all
  rows, keep label/value columns together, let tables flow vertically, separate
  independent tables and protect the shared heading. Recreate with
  `generate-auto-tables.py` (requires openpyxl and Pillow).
- `excel-auto-objects.xlsx`: adjacent structured Excel tables and a separate
  worksheet with a graphic spanning two column groups. Native inspection must
  separate the table objects, retain every row, and keep all graphic-sheet
  columns together with the image still painted. Generated by the same script.

Their identical stems intentionally exercise output-name collision handling.

## Legacy fixtures

On 2026-10-13, the installed Microsoft Office 16.113.4 apps saved private copies
of the OOXML fixtures as genuine binary Office files:

- Word: `sample.doc`, using `format document97`.
- Excel: `sample.xls` and `multiple-sheets.xls`, using `Excel98to2004 file format`.
- PowerPoint: `sample.ppt`, using `save as presentation`.

`legacy-provenance.json` records source/output SHA-256 hashes, app versions,
export commands, and verification of the binary compound-file header. These
are not renamed OOXML files. All document content is synthetic; Office writes
its normal author and application metadata during saving.

`python3 tests/fixtures/generate-legacy.py` reproduces this process on macOS,
using the installed apps and the already-approved CLI staging folder. It
refuses to overwrite existing fixtures; move those four binary fixtures aside
before deliberately regenerating them. The regular tests use the saved files
and do not regenerate them.
